A simulated habitat-selection study on Stoney Lake

Source: R/data.R
stoney_selection.Rd

Forty animals tracked for 48 hours from 00:00 UTC on 1 June 2024 on the 70 receivers of stoney_track, with a known preference for bottom depth. The animals walk the correlated random walk of stoney_track (steps of mean 30 m and SD 15 m a minute, turns of SD 40 degrees), and each step is accepted in proportion to exp(beta x bottom depth in m), so beta is a selection coefficient per step. selection-01 to selection-20 have beta = -0.3 per m, a preference for shallow water; selection-21 to selection-40 have beta = 0, no preference. Both groups start from the same 20 water cells. Tags send every 120 to 180 s, and detections are drawn from the range model of stoney_track with no variation between receivers or hours.

Usage

stoney_selection

Format

A list:

receivers

The 70 receivers of stoney_track.

detections

27,442 detections in the 48 hours: datetime, receiver_serial, transmitter, animal_id.

tags

One row per animal, 40 rows: transmitter, animal_id, beta, replicate (the animal's number, 1 to 20 within each beta; the same number marks the same start cell), min_delay, max_delay.

track

The true position each minute, 115,240 rows (2,881 per animal): animal_id, datetime, cell, the cell of the lake raster the animal was in, and x and y, the simulated position in metres (UTM 17N), kept to within 10 m of it, toward the centre of its cell.

presence

The position draws of the trial, 35,700 rows: 20 cells per detected hour (1,785 hours) drawn with sample_locations() from the hourly surfaces of the field the detections were drawn from: the draws the trial analysed for these animals. Columns and attributes as sample_locations() returns them.

coverage

A list of two system_de() tables, date, cell and p, for the three UTC days of the study and the 4,818 water cells: transmission, the probability that one transmission is detected, and hour, the probability that an hour of 24 transmissions is.

truth

The settings: layer, betas, hours, movement, tag delay, transmissions per hour (24), position draws and available points per stratum (20 each), and the seeds of both blocks, for reproducing them.

trial

3,144 rows, one per block, animal, beta, array, availability and source, for detected hours: block (1 or 2); beta; receivers (70 or 20); availability, drawn from the whole detection surface: "weighted" (in proportion to the hourly detection probability), "per_transmission" (in proportion to the per-transmission probability), "uniform_0.1" or "uniform_0.2" (uniform over cells heard with that probability or more per transmission); source ("truth", every third minute of the true track, or "positions", the position draws); animal (the replicate); estimate and se, the conditional logit coefficient for bottom depth per m pooled over 20 imputations with Rubin's rules; n_hours, the animal's detected hours; single_share, the share of them heard by one receiver; and warned, TRUE when an imputation fit warned (separation). Animals never heard have no rows: 4 of 100 on 20 receivers in block 1 and 3 in block 2.

hours

8,872 rows, one per detected hour of the trial's animals on 70 receivers, both blocks: block, beta, animal, bin_start, receivers (receivers that heard the animal in the hour), true_m and drawn_m, the mean bottom depth in m of the hour's 20 true points and of its 20 position draws.

Source

Simulated with the walk, tag and detection simulators of the arraydesign R package on the Stoney raster and the range model of stoney_track (the raster's source is under stoney_track), then positioned and analysed with this package's own functions. The script that builds it is https://github.com/jakebrownscombe/detfield/blob/main/data-raw/stoney_selection.R, and https://github.com/jakebrownscombe/detfield/blob/main/data-raw/stoney_selection_track_xy.R adds the positions of track. Both are in the repository and not in the installed package. The scripts rebuild the study and the draws; they copy trial and hours from the outputs of the trial, which was run outside the package, and those outputs are not in the repository.

Details

The study is part of a trial of 20 animals at each of five betas (-0.3, -0.1, 0, 0.1 and 0.3) on two arrays, the 70 receivers of stoney_track and 20 receivers on a regular grid (the array of arraydesign's examples), in which the depth coefficient from position draws was set against the same coefficient from the true track. The trial was run on two disjoint blocks of animals; block 2 has its own starts, tracks and detections. Within a block the five betas share start cells. The forty animals here are block 1's at beta -0.3 and 0 on 70 receivers, so the analysis of the article vignette("habitat-selection") reproduces their rows of trial.

See also

sample_available(), used_available(), stoney_track

Examples

table(stoney_selection$tags$beta)
#> 
#> -0.3    0 
#>   20   20 
# Population mean of the per-animal coefficients in block 1 of the trial
block1 <- stoney_selection$trial[stoney_selection$trial$block == 1 &
                                   stoney_selection$trial$availability ==
                                     "weighted", ]
aggregate(estimate ~ receivers + source + beta, data = block1, FUN = mean)[1:10, ]
#>    receivers    source beta     estimate
#> 1         20 positions -0.3 -0.436289696
#> 2         70 positions -0.3 -0.077022788
#> 3         20     truth -0.3 -0.886205221
#> 4         70     truth -0.3 -0.150405629
#> 5         20 positions -0.1 -0.011184447
#> 6         70 positions -0.1 -0.025134357
#> 7         20     truth -0.1 -0.044941015
#> 8         70     truth -0.1 -0.077556091
#> 9         20 positions  0.0 -0.430920434
#> 10        70 positions  0.0 -0.009602902
# Position draws minus true position, bottom depth (m), per detected hour
hours <- stoney_selection$hours
tapply(hours$drawn_m - hours$true_m, hours$block, mean)
#>         1         2 
#> 0.3403630 0.3533513
